scope: Primary-source quantitative follow-up for continual_learning CLG1-CL-005/006 and long_horizon LH-Context-Folding.

supersedes_assessments.mechanism: Infinite learning-rate schedule to avoid repeated cosine re-warming in continual pre-training

quantitative_results: Small-scale CIFAR-10 MAE without replay: infinite cosine improves average accuracy by 1.87 percentage points and BWT by about 4 points over repeated cosine.
Large-scale MAE aggregate metrics with 5% experience replay: repeated cosine Avg Acc/BWT 48.87/-3.61 versus infinite cosine 50.18/-1.37. Without replay: 39.69/-17.91 versus 41.22/-15.06.
Additional across-time forgetting metrics with 5% replay: repeated cosine Overall Acc 44.76, REM 97.11, Overall BWT -2.89, CL score 37.96; infinite cosine 50.56, 99.54, -0.46, 40.61.

For autoregressive LM continual pre-training, the paper reports better upstream validation retention under infinite schedules and zero-shot averages that favor infinite cosine in the DCLM -> Stack setting. With 50% replay, the best table-3 average is 46.81 for infinite cosine eta_const=2e-4 versus 44.65 for repeated cosine after DCLM -> Stack -> German; on German-specific ARC-de/HellaSwag-de, the best average is only 28.10 versus cosine 28.09, so newest-domain adaptation gains there are negligible.
causal_or_design_checks: The matched comparison changes the learning-rate schedule while holding continual pre-training setup fixed, with explicit with/without replay conditions.

Appendix checkpoint-selection ablation compares infinite cosine against repeated-cosine restarts from two manually selected high-LR checkpoints; infinite cosine still yields consistently lower linear-probe loss, reducing the alternative explanation that checkpoint choice alone drives the effect.
Replay interaction is nontrivial: higher eta_const can improve adaptability when replay is present, while lower eta_const better preserves earlier knowledge without replay.
primary_verification.scope: Strong evidence that repeated re-warming is avoidable and that an infinite schedule can improve stability in the studied SSL/LM continual-pretraining regimes. It is not evidence for a universal fixed eta_const; tuning remains distribution- and replay-dependent.

supersedes_assessments.judgment: Upgrade B -> A-. Exact primary quantitative tables, replay interactions, checkpoint-control analysis, peer-reviewed venue, and public code are now verified. The intervention is low-complexity and well matched, but the language-model newest-domain effect can be tiny and no independent replication was established in this pass.

supersedes_assessments.mechanism: Model-time replay scheduling plus intensity-aware replay regularization (FOREVER)

primary_verification.protocol: All methods use the same LoRA-based framework and same number of epochs; main experiments are averaged over three independent runs and multiple task orders.

qwen3_0_6b_table.Memory-Based: FOREVER OP/BWT 72.9/-4.7 versus VBM 71.5/-5.2, AIMMerging 71.9/-5.0, Recurrent-KIF 70.6/-6.5

primary_verification.aggregate: Paper reports average OP +1.2 points and BWT +0.9 points over the prior best VBM across the three benchmark columns.
primary_verification.model_scale: On SuperNI with LLaMA3.1-8B, FOREVER improves OP 49.0 -> 50.6 and BWT -2.9 -> -2.1 versus VBM; the study covers 0.6B to 13B backbones.
primary_verification.component_ablation: Primary Table 2 separately removes/replaces replay scheduler and intensity-aware regularization. The paper also compares fixed-interval, reversed, and end-only replay schedules and alternative regularizers, providing direct mechanism-level controls rather than headline-only comparison.
primary_verification.failure_scope: The gains over the strongest Ebbinghaus-style VBM baseline are consistent but modest. Evidence supports model-update-based replay timing and adaptive replay strength in the tested LoRA continual-learning settings, not a claim that human forgetting curves are universally optimal for arbitrary learning systems.

supersedes_assessments.judgment: Upgrade B -> A. The previously unverified secondary 61.5 aggregate is no longer needed: the archival primary provides complete per-benchmark OP/BWT tables, three-run protocol, cross-scale evidence, direct ablations, and public code. This is strong scoped evidence for model-centric replay timing plus adaptive replay strength; the modest effect size versus VBM should be preserved.

supersedes_assessments.mechanism: Learned branch-and-fold context management with FoldGRPO

controls: Same Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct base, data, infrastructure, and RL hyperparameters are used for the directly comparable ReAct and folding baselines.

FoldGRPO vs standard GRPO improves folding-agent pass@1 from 0.567 to 0.620 on BrowseComp-Plus and 0.564 to 0.580 on SWE-Bench, isolating value from the process-reward/context-aware RL formulation beyond folding architecture alone.

Behavior ablation: BrowseComp Finish/MainLen/Scope changes 0.738/22,285/0.762 under standard GRPO to 0.935/7,752/0.895 under FoldGRPO; SWE changes 0.612/48,908/0.419 to 0.962/8,885/0.754, showing over-90% main-context compression with better branch focus/completion.
scope: The 10x claim is peak active context (32K) versus the 327K long-context ReAct baseline; folding can consume up to 32K x 10 total branch budget, so it is not a 10x total-token/computation saving claim.
Untrained folding beats matched 32K ReAct and summarization baselines but remains below 327K ReAct; the strongest result requires RL and FoldGRPO.

The public repository states that it is an open-source reimplementation and may differ from the code used to train the paper model; full validation of training results is/was still in progress. No independent headline replication was established here.

supersedes_assessments.judgment: Upgrade C -> A-. Exact primary task-level numbers and mechanism/behavior ablations are now verified. Evidence strongly supports learned context folding as a way to preserve a small active working context while retaining long-horizon performance in the two tested domains, but the result should not be misreported as a 10x total-compute reduction and remains preprint-level without independent replication.

important_scope_corrections: FOREVER: preserve the small margin over VBM; do not rely on the earlier secondary 61.5 aggregate when full primary per-benchmark table is available.
Context-Folding: 10x smaller active context does not mean 10x lower total token use; branch budget can reach 32K x 10 and FoldGRPO increases tool use/exploration.

Infinite schedule: language newest-domain adaptation advantage can be negligible; the stronger evidence is retention/stability and replay-dependent tradeoff, not universal superiority on every downstream metric.
